business_scope.primary_industry_name: Rotocasting Injection and Airbrush Finishing of Vinyl Art Collectibles

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 2009, in force 2010)
Switzerland–United States Double Taxation Convention (as amended by 2010 Protocol)
Switzerland–Hong Kong, China Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (signed 2013)
European Free Trade Association (EFTA) Convention (Switzerland as founding member)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0) and its implementing Ordinance (AMLO, SR 955.01); Swiss Code of Obligations (CO) articles 622, 626 and 697j regarding bearer shares and beneficial owners; Ordinance on the Commercial Register (ORC) and the Federal Act on the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMASA) for KYC/AML standards; Directive of the Federal Office of Justice on the Register of Beneficial Owners (which is not publicly accessible).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport for each director, founder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport issuing authority of the country of citizenship or permanent residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostilled certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating commercial register or registrar of companies outside Switzerland

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney for incorporation and certified signature specimen (for local signatory or agent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary or authorized foreign notary/public under the Hague Apostille Convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Security Council consolidated list, Swiss SECO economic sanctions and asset freezes, EU restrictive measures insofar as adopted by Switzerland, the U.S. OFAC SDN List, and the UK consolidated sanctions list. Additional enhanced due diligence is statutorily required for politically exposed persons (PEPs) under AMLA and FINMA Circular 2017/06 on KYC duties, including identity verification, source-of-wealth assessment, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Every proposed name clearance must also be screened for apparent UBO ties to sanctioned jurisdictions or listed persons.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zentraler Firmenindex (ZEFIX) of the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregister / Registre du Commerce) maintained by the Federal Commercial Registry Office under the Federal Office of Justice
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be written in one of the Swiss national languages (German, French, Italian, or Romansh) using Latin script, unless the name has a distinctly international character. The name must not be misleading, contrary to public order, or infringe third-party rights. Non-Latin-script foreign corporate names may require phonetic or official transliteration into a Swiss language, and the commercial register accepts only exact Latin-script transliterations that permit clear identification.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss, Schweizer, Suisse, Svizzero, Eidgenössisch, Bund, Confederation (requiring special authorization)
Anwalt, Rechtsanwalt, Notar, Patentanwalt, Fiduziar (regulated professions)
AG, SA, Ltd, Corporation, Incorporated (used solely as legal form suffix per CO Art. 950)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the commercial registry office of the canton in which incorporation is sought, within 30 days from the date of written notice. The appeal is transmitted to the cantonal commercial registry supervisory authority or, where applicable, the cantonal court with commercial jurisdiction. A rejected reservation can be replaced by filing a new reservation immediately; the initial 90-day reservation may be extended for a further 90 days where the rejection appeal is pending, provided the extension fee is paid before expiry. The final decision of the supervisory authority may be subject to appeal to the Federal Administrative Court for errors of law.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office consisting of a mere mailing address or remote-only presence is not permissible. The Swiss registered office must be a physical address in Switzerland at which the company may be reached during business hours and where administration records are available for inspection. For a low-risk designer-toy merchandising entity, a licensed commercial domiciliation company or fiduciary providing a physical office, letterhead, lawful contact point, and administrative agent is accepted, subject to the rules of the commercial register and cantonal practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate for a non-regulated online merchandising business; approximately 5–15% per year for an unannounced on-site inspection by tax authorities, commercial-register inspectors, or social-security control authorities, and 2–5% where a licensed domiciliation provider maintains the registered office and full legal records.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry fee for the new AG

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization fees for foreign passport and shareholder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent issuing authority in country of origin (e.g., Ministry of Foreign Affairs) and/or Swiss embassy/consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory apostille fee per document (typically CHF 20–50) plus courier and translation vendor fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of articles of association and foreign corporate documents into a Swiss official language
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator or Swiss translation agency

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed domiciliation / registered-office service for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed commercial domiciliation provider or fiduciary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for paid domiciliation and administration services in Switzerland (CHF 120–180 per month)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax and VAT registration administrative fee (Federal Tax Administration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official administrative fee for federal and cantonal tax registration (CHF 40–60)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting and review of articles of association, shareholders' agreements, and name clearance application
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat market benchmark for incorporation of an AG with UBO and AML documentation (CHF 1,400–2,200)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO screening, PEP and sanctions database checks, and KYC file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance provider or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per full electronic screening and verification package (CHF 500–800)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR) Arts. 620-640 (stock company incorporation), Arts. 643-644 (registration and publicity), and Arts. 640-641 (organs and auditors); Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV) Arts. 18-29 and 76-80
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (Gründungsurkunde) with Articles of Association (Statuten), submitted as the application for entry in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum share capital is CHF 100,000; at least 20% (CHF 20,000) must be fully paid up in cash before registration. The paid-up amount must be deposited in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a licensed Swiss bank and released only upon presentation of the Commercial Register extract evidencing registration; in-kind contributions require a statutory audit report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company's incorporation having been completed by notarial deed, the Board of Directors: (1) confirms the subscription and allotment of the share capital and acknowledges the deposit of the legally paid-up minimum portion in the blocked escrow account; (2) adopts the address stated in the Articles of Association as the registered office in the Canton of Zug; (3) appoints [Name] Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] Chairman of the Board, with recorded signature authority; (4) authorizes the Chairman and the Chief Executive Officer, jointly, to execute the Commercial Register application and related filings; and (5) resolves that the Company commences operations only upon its entry in the Commercial Register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparatory drafting and name clearance of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public licensed in the Canton of Zug; Company Name Office of the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the notary to draft the founding documents, including the Articles of Association, subscriber list and any in-kind contribution agreement; simultaneously apply for name clearance with the Commercial Register to confirm the legal availability and distinctiveness of the proposed corporate name 'CH_AG' variant before notarization.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each natural-person founder
Proof of address for the proposed registered office in Zug
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
Name reservation confirmation from the Commercial Register
Founder declarations on in-kind contributions or special privileges, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, amend the name and resubmit within 10 days; the notarial deed must not be executed under a disputed name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the blocked escrow account and deposit of minimum paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss licensed bank with branch in Canton Zug (e.g. Zuger Kantonalbank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the company being formed; deposit at least CHF 20,000 in cash contributions; obtain the bank's written confirmation that funds are irrevocably held and blocked until presentation of the final Commercial Register excerpt; alternatively, in-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's valuation certificate.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Notary engagement letter or draft foundation deed
Identification documents of the account signatories
Beneficial ownership declaration (Form A) for AML compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML queries, provide a sworn declaration of source of funds and resume the process; if still refused, transfer the escrow mandate to another licensed Swiss bank without loss of the deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial deed of incorporation and constitutive general meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public in the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the notarial deed of incorporation before the notary; hold the constitutive general meeting; formally adopt the Articles of Association; appoint the board of directors and, unless the audit opt-out under Art. 727a(2) OR is declared, appoint the statutory auditor; the minutes and deed must be executed in notarized form.
required_dossiers: Name clearance confirmation
Bank escrow deposit confirmation
Subscriber list with allocated shares and nominal values
Signed Articles of Association
Statutory auditor's report on in-kind contributions, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect, cure it by obtaining the missing confirmation and re-scheduling the notarization; no statutory deadline is missed, but pre-agreed completion interest may accrue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting, appointments and signatory registration formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Aktiengesellschaft; notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene and hold the first board meeting adopting the pro-forma first board resolution; determine the organization; appoint the Chairman, Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer with defined signing authority; decide on audit opt-out thresholds; record the minutes and certify them for later submission to the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution
Written acceptance declarations of newly appointed officers and board members
Declaration of related-party transactions, if any
Written record of the audit opt-out decision
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an appointment is challenged or invalid, the shareholders' meeting may re-elect the officer and a corrected notarized minute must be filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for entry in the Commercial Register and completion of legal personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the registration application electronically via the EHRA portal or in paper form with original notarial signatures; attach the notarial deed, Articles of Association, escrow release bank confirmation, list of directors with signatory authority, and the declaration of compliance; the AG acquires legal personality upon the Commercial Register entry and publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
required_dossiers: Notarized registration application form
Notarial deed of incorporation
Certified copy of the Articles of Association
Bank confirmation of escrow deposit and release instruction
List of authorized signatories with signature specimen
Payment confirmation of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registrar issues an interim query, respond within 10 days with exigible documents; a rejection notice may be appealed to the Cantonal Court of Zug within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, social security and employer registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration Zug (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung Zug); Federal Social Insurance Compensation Office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse); SUVA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Commercial Register extract, apply for corporate income tax, VAT and UID number; register as employer with the AHV-Ausgleichskasse and obtain the employer number; register with SUVA for mandatory accident insurance; perform cantonal statistical registration; secure fire safety, environmental and workplace permits before operating.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract and UID number certificate
Lease agreement for the registered office in Zug
Passport copies of all board members and authorized signatories
Employer registration form for AHV and SUVA
Cantonal tax declaration and permanent establishment information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office or compensation office requests additional documentation, respond within 30 days; estimated provisional filings prevent late-interest exposure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sectoral industrial license is required for rotocasting and vinyl toy manufacturing under Swiss trade freedom (Art. 27 Federal Constitution); the relevant oversight authorities are the Cantonal Labor Inspectorate of Zug (Arbeitsinspektorat) and SUVA for workplace safety, with municipal building permit authority for the production premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required - activity is license-free; a municipal building permit (Baugesuch) and cantonal fire safety approval are required for the physical manufacturing site.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU) with cantonal execution by the Office of Environment of the Canton of Zug (Amt für Umweltschutz Zug)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - preliminary screening (Voruntersuchung) under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV/OEIE); a full EIA report is not mandatory for a small-scale vinyl rotocasting plant, but the facility must obtain an operating permit for VOC and wastewater emissions under the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) and Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with GSchV, COD limit up to 25 mg/L and prohibition of hazardous substance discharge into water; exhaust air: VOC concentration limit of 20 mg/m3 for airbrush and paint finishing ventilation with odour control; waste: PVC residues, spray booth filters and solvent waste classified and handled under the Ordinance on Movements of Waste (VEVA) as hazardous where applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Fire Prevention Office of the Canton of Zug (Feuerpolizei) for the production premises; structural load inspection in accordance with SIA 261 standards; workplace clearance and mandatory accident insurance confirmation (AGR number) issued by SUVA, with occupational health verification for solvent handling areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions, AFC), VAT Division (Hauptabteilung Mehrwertsteuer); official portal: www.estv.admin.ch; UID registry: www.uid.admin.ch; e-filing: www.estv.admin.ch/e-services. Cantonal authorities (e.g., Tax Administration of Canton Zug) assess corporate income tax on federal and cantonal/municipal levels; VAT is exclusively a federal tax administered by the ESTV.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Notarise the AG deed and file it with the Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt); the company automatically receives the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, e.g., CHE-123.456.789), while the minimum capital of CHF 100,000 (at least CHF 50,000 paid in) must be evidenced. Step 2: Register for Swiss VAT with the ESTV via Form 101 or the secure FTA e-portal when worldwide taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per annum; the ESTV then issues the VAT number 'CHE-123.456.789 MWST'. Step 3: A foreign entity with neither registered office nor place of business in Switzerland that owes Swiss VAT must appoint a tax representative (Steuervertreter) under Art. 67 MWSTG and register before supplying taxable services/goods in Switzerland. Step 4: The AG must additionally register with the competent cantonal tax office for corporate income and capital tax assessment, which is verified against the Commercial Register entry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the Swiss AG is an independent corporate taxpayer subject to federal income tax at 8.5% (after deducting the federal tax itself from the base), plus cantonal and municipal income taxes (combined effective rates typically 11.5%–21%, approximately 14.6% in Zug), and capital tax on equity. A resident AG is taxable on worldwide profits, with territorial allocation/exemption for foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate; pass-through treatment is unavailable for an AG.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime exists in Switzerland; a Swiss AG is a per se corporation under US Treas. Reg. §301.7701-2(b)(8), so no US disregarded-entity election is possible. Elections available under Swiss law include: (i) automatic participation exemption (Beteiligungsabzug) for qualifying dividends and capital gains on substantial holdings; (ii) notional interest deduction (NID) on excess equity, available in adopting cantons such as Zug; (iii) patent box relief and additional R&D super-deduction under TRAF 2020; (iv) depreciation methodology elections and accelerated write-offs; (v) hybrid mismatch outcomes are constrained by general anti-abuse rules, the Swiss participation exemption conditions, and treaty provisions – no formal hybrid-mismatch election exists, and Switzerland has no group taxation consolidation election for income tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) pursuant to the Swiss VAT Act of 12 June 2009 (MWSTG, SR 641.20)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 worldwide gross taxable turnover per fiscal year (Art. 10 MWSTG), effective 1 January 2025 increased to CHF 250,000; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold, and small businesses with turnover not exceeding the threshold may claim simplified exemption relief (Art. 109 MWSTG).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has no real-time fiscal clearance, API-based approval, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping for VAT. Invoices need only satisfy Art. 26 MWSTG content requirements (names, VAT numbers, date, description, rate, amount) and may be issued in paper or electronic form. The QR-bill and eBill standards (Swiss Payment Standards 2024) are widely used and the ESTV accepts electronic archives, while Peppol-based exchange is emerging for public procurement; no government pre-clearance or cryptographic stamping is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rate (0% VAT with full input tax deduction) applies to: (i) export of goods to a foreign country where the goods are physically transported abroad (Art. 23(1) MWSTG); (ii) services directly connected with exported goods, including transport and logistics (Art. 23(2)); (iii) specified services rendered to foreign customers, such as licensing of intellectual property and consultancy supplied from Switzerland (Art. 23(3)). For designer blind-box toys (ISIC 3240), only actual physical exports of finished collectibles from Switzerland qualify for the 0% rate; domestic sales are taxable at 8.1%, and consignment transfers to EU fulfilment centres do not qualify as final exports and trigger local VAT registration obligations. Export evidence must exist at the time the VAT return is filed and must be retained for ten years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss customs export declaration (e-dec electronic declaration with movement reference number) and the stamped export certificate (Ausfuhrschein)
Bill of Lading (B/L), air waybill (AWB), or CMR consignment note naming the foreign consignee and destination port
Inward remittance certificate or SWIFT bank confirmation evidencing payment in foreign currency and FX repatriation
Commercial invoice stating Incoterms, declared customs value, full product description, and HS code 9503.00
Packing list, container manifest, and transport insurance certificate covering the export leg
For services exports: signed declaration from the foreign recipient confirming its foreign residence and the actual use/destination of the service outside Switzerland
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV routinely audits export files; missing, incomplete, or falsified export proofs cause re-taxation of the supply at the standard 8.1% rate, with input VAT clawback, default interest, and possible retrospective adjustment of prior tax periods. Negligent tax evasion (Art. 102 MWSTG) incurs a fine of up to 300% of the tax evaded; wilful VAT or customs fraud (Art. 103, Abgabebetrug) may lead to imprisonment for up to five years and a fine of up to 400% of the evaded tax; procedural retention violations (Art. 105 MWSTG) are fined up to CHF 8,000. The 180-day FX repatriation figure is a Swiss banking and export-compliance convention rather than a statutory VAT requirement, because Switzerland has no mandatory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; nevertheless, Swiss banks and export credit insurers treat 180 days as the standard payment settlement norm for documenting completed export transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse), headquartered in Bern and Zurich, operating under Article 99 of the Federal Constitution. Banking and AML conduct supervision is exercised by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA); residual sanctions administration and export controls rest with the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc (CHF) enjoys full current and capital account convertibility consistent with Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. Switzerland imposes no exchange controls, no capital-flow restrictions, no mandatory FX conversion regime, and no central bank authorization requirement for foreign direct investment, dividend remittance, royalty payments, or intercompany financing. The only structural profit-remittance friction is Swiss withholding tax of 35% on dividend distributions, which is frequently reduced to 0% to 5% under Switzerland's double tax treaty network or eliminated within Swiss groups, while the separate issuance tax and certain interest withholding tax points were dismantled under the 2023 corporate tax reform. No inward investment screening applies to a designer-toy manufacturing and merchandising entity, although banking due diligence will require documented source-of-funds and beneficial ownership evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Swiss law imposes no statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Exporters are freely entitled to retain, remit, convert, or hold export proceeds in any currency without FINMA or SNB permission, and there is no repatriation or liquidation obligation. The SNB collects only statistical balance-of-payments data: banks report cross-border payment flows on behalf of clients, and a resident enterprise with material aggregate cross-border payments (typically above the SNB's published entity-level reporting threshold, where direct reporting forms apply) must file statistical returns. No FX surrender or export-conversion duty exists.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for Swiss-licensed fintechs and payment service providers (FINMA banking license under the FinTech Ordinance / Art. 1b Banking Act, public deposit cap of CHF 100 million, no interest on deposits), but Low for offshore digital EMIs (UK FCA EMIs or EU PSD2 EMIs). Offshore EMIs have no passporting rights into Switzerland, no SIC interbank clearing access, and cannot issue Swiss IBAN accounts for domestic settlement or accept Swiss retail deposits without a Swiss banking or AMLA financial-intermediary license. For the target payment rails (Shopify Payments, Stripe, Local POS), the compliant architecture is a Swiss merchant acquiring agreement with a FINMA-supervised PSP and final settlement into a Swiss tier-1 bank account; an offshore EMI may serve only as an auxiliary receiving corridor if its underlying provider is registered under Art. 20 AMLA, and never as the primary treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandated for non-Swiss-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners. AMLA and FINMA Circular 2016/7 (CDB 20) require banks to verify the identity and beneficial ownership of all authorized signatories; remote video identification is accepted only within bank-specific programmes restricted to Swiss residents or, at certain FINMA-regulated banks, to EU/EEA residents using government-certified identity verification. For a foreign-owned CH_AG with non-resident principals, an in-person onboarding interview at a Swiss branch (Zurich or Zug) or before a Swiss consulate/notary is the prevailing standard. An in-person board meeting in Switzerland to approve account mandates simultaneously supports Swiss economic substance, payroll, and the documentary substance file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign directorship and non-resident UBO — red flags on residence, tax domicile, and remoteness of control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized corporate documents of CH_AG (Articles of Association, Swiss Commercial Register excerpt), foreign parent organizational chart, certified UBO self-declaration, passport copies of all directors and shareholders, apostilled proof of domicile, board resolution appointing Swiss-resident signatories where practicable, and a substance file proving physical office, Swiss payroll, and real decision-making in Zug.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth opacity for the initial CHF capital injection (personal savings, crypto gains, or IP/NFT proceeds of the founder).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements covering the prior 12 to 24 months, sale and purchase contracts for IP/NFT/art assets, escrow settlement reports, digital-asset exchange withdrawal logs with blockchain tracing report if requested, tax returns and tax-assessment notices of the contributing shareholder, notarized gift or inheritance deeds, and a written source-of-funds letter aligned with the bank's CDB 20 template.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce volume volatility — Shopify/Stripe payout spikes versus declared revenue, refunds, and cross-border platform collection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Marketplace settlement files (Shopify Payments and Stripe payout reports), transactional order-level export, refund and chargeback logs, shipping and customs declarations, Swiss and foreign VAT/MWST filings, inventory purchasing records, ERP revenue reconciliation, audited annual financial statements, and merchant verification certificates from the payment platforms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned-country exposure — consumers or wholesale distributors in restricted territories (e.g., Russia, Belarus, Iran, Syria, North Korea) or payment-card issuing countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions screening outputs (SECO, UN, and EU-adopted lists), geo-blocking and IP-filter configuration evidence, prohibitive shipping terms in the online terms of service, restricted-country blacklists embedded in Shopify/Stripe configurations, negative-match declarations by sales agents, and a sanctions compliance policy manual consistent with FINMA guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or adverse-media hit on a minority shareholder, nominee director, or authorized representative.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified PEP and adverse-media screening reports (World-Check or Dow Jones), biographical profile and explanation letter, disassociation or mitigation resolution approved by the bank's senior management, relationship risk-assessment template, and, if applicable, replacement of the affected signatory to remove the trigger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual intercompany or royalty flows — payments to an IP-holding affiliate without apparent business purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed intercompany license agreements, transfer pricing documentation (OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines; arm's-length royalty rate benchmarking), IP registration records (Federal Institute of Intellectual Property), valuation report of the brand or toy-character IP, board minutes approving the license, intercompany payment flow chart, and allocable substance evidence of the licensor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR) to the Swiss capital escrow account at a tier-1 bank (UBS or ZKB), with the mandatory wire narrative 'Share capital contribution / Liberierung Aktien / CH_AG' and explicit reference to the bank's escrow deposit certificate. The deposit must satisfy the statutory incorporation verification under Art. 632 of the Swiss Code of Obligations (minimum share capital CHF 100,000 with at least 20% of the nominal value of each share paid in cash before registration). Switzerland does not operate a national purpose-code authority; for SEPA ISO 20022 payments, the ExternalPurpose code 'EQUI' (equity) or 'INTC' (intra-company) is commonly used, and the exact accepted code must be confirmed with the receiving bank. For CNY-denominated inbound flows, routing via CIPS or through the Swiss bank's offshore CNH desk is recommended. All wires must be matched to the notarized capital increase resolution and the certified UBO declarations to withstand AML review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to Chinese, Southeast Asian, and European manufacturers use SWIFT MT103 for USD/EUR wires via the Swiss bank's correspondent network, with Incoterms-compliant shipping documents. For large or consignment production runs, confirmed documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT740) drawn on Swiss banks with China desks are preferred. EUR payments clear via SEPA (ISO 20022 pain.001, purpose code 'SUPP'); CHF domestic payments clear via the SIX SIC interbank system; USD wires run through CHIPS or Fedwire via the New York correspondent; CNY payments settle through offshore CNH clearing or CIPS. Shopify Payments and Stripe payouts aggregate settlement balances into the Swiss operational account by standard SEPA/MT103 credit transfers; local POS transactions (Visa/Mastercard) settle through Swiss acquiring banks directly into the same account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Over-the-counter outright FX forwards (Devisentermingeschäft) with Swiss banks in CHF/USD/EUR/CNH, maturity up to 12 months, documented under an ISDA FX Master Agreement or bank-specific FX confirmation.
FX swaps (Devisenswaps) for short-term liquidity management in CHF, USD, and EUR.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on offshore RMB (CNH) and other restricted/emerging-market currencies through London or New York counterparties, given onshore CNY non-deliverability for non-resident corporate hedgers.
Cross-currency swaps (Währungsswaps) for treasury and debt-related operations, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex.

Plain-vanilla European-style FX options for strategic procurement-risk hedging, subject to the Financial Market Infrastructure Act (FinMIA) derivative rules and professional-client classification; speculative transaction positions are expressly excluded by the treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal, cantonal and communal annual tax return (annual fiscal declaration) together with the AG's annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority of the registered office (Kantonssteueramt); Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) receives the federal direct tax component through the cantonal declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the close of the statutory financial year; calendar-year companies ordinarily file by 30 June of the following year; written extensions are available from the cantonal authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest accrues from 30 days after the final assessment (canton-specific rate approximately 5% p.a.); procedural fines for late or incomplete filing may reach CHF 10,000; deliberate incompleteness constitutes tax evasion. Persistent insolvency and failure to deal with liabilities can ultimately trigger administrative strike-off through the Commercial Register Office.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT return (MWST-Abrechnung) covering the reporting period of the AG's trading activity in designer toys and art collectibles
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the assigned VAT settlement period; annual settlement for taxable persons below CHF 5 million annual turnover with calendar-year due date, quarterly settlement above that threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may attract a summary fine of up to CHF 8,000 plus default interest at 5% p.a.; deliberate misdeclaration is prosecuted as tax transgression. VAT arrears are not a direct commercial register strike-off ground.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AHV/IV/EO/ALV employer social security declaration and final contribution settlement for all employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Compensation Fund (Ausgleichskasse) selected for the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of the calendar year for annual wage reporting; employers with higher payrolls must render quarterly or semi-annual provisional settlements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears of social security contributions carry statutory default interest; late declaration can attract administrative fines and, in willful cases, criminal sanctions. Non-payment alone does not directly cause strike-off but may be considered in insolvency proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting package: adopted annual financial statements, appropriation of profit, discharge of directors, and auditor's report where audit is mandatory or shareholder-elected
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with a regulatory authority; adopted records retained at the registered office, made available to shareholders, and submitted as part of the annual tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The ordinary shareholders' meeting must be held and financial statements adopted within 6 months of the AG's balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM allows shareholders to obtain a judicial convocation order; a dormant AG that cannot be organized may be declared organizationally defective by the Commercial Register Office and ultimately struck off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual internal register audit: verification of the share register (Aktienbuch), beneficial owner register, board minutes and capital structure accuracy, with a written review concluded before the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors; statutory auditor if appointed; beneficial owner register is available for inspection by the Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS) and tax authorities upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the annual general meeting each year; registered share transfers must be recorded immediately, with consent decisions documented without delay
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Breaches are administrative violations under the Swiss Code of Obligations and Anti-Money Laundering Act; corrective orders and fines can be imposed by supervisory or criminal authorities, although no automatic strike-off is triggered.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (full) audit is required where the AG exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets above CHF 20 million, annual revenue above CHF 40 million, or annual average of 250 employees. Simplified audit is required where two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: total assets above CHF 4 million, annual revenue above CHF 8 million, or annual average of 50 employees. Below the simplified thresholds an AG may dispense with audit entirely upon the unanimous decision of all shareholders, provided no shareholder has demanded an audit in accordance with Art. 727a OR.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting provisions (Art. 957 et seq. OR); Swiss GAAP FER is the generally recognized local framework; IFRS is expressly permitted and is practically mandatory for listed companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland maintains no public beneficial-ownership register. The AG must keep an internal register of beneficial owners under Art. 626a OR and the Anti-Money Laundering Act, situated at the registered office. There is no annual external filing requirement; the Board reviews and confirms the register's accuracy at least once each calendar year and contemporaneously records every transfer of registered shares and any change in beneficial ownership. Authorized authorities may inspect the register during statutory or tax proceedings.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Board Functions
Register of Beneficial Owners (internal GwG/AML register)
Minute Book of Board of Directors' Meetings
Accounting records and vouchers for at least 7 years

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 to USD 4,000 per year for registered office, annual compliance mailbox, and regulatory agent services; Zug and Zurich charge at the higher end of the range.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 to USD 9,000 for a simplified audit; USD 13,000 to USD 42,000 for an ordinary audit depending on complexity, number of shareholders, and entity structure.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Swiss federal corporate income tax (Erwerbssteuer) 8.5% flat rate imposed on after-tax profit; approximately 7.83% on pre-tax profit. Combined federal + cantonal/communal statutory headline rate for an Aktiengesellschaft domiciled in the Zug benchmark location: 14.6% (Federal 8.5% + Zug cantonal/communal 6.1% on taxable earnings before federal tax).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (STAF, effective 1 January 2020): Patent box/IP relief reducing qualifying IP income by up to 90%; qualifying R&D additional deduction of 50% of R&D costs (capped at 80% of taxable income); participation deduction of 95-100% for qualifying dividend and capital gains income; notional interest deduction (NDID) on qualifying borrowings; hidden-reserve relief on deemed liquidation; cantonal innovation incentives and, in selected cantons, time-limited tax holidays for newly created substance-generating activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined federal and cantonal corporate income tax return: 'Steuererklärung für juristische Personen / Formulaire fiscal pour les personnes morales' (corporate 'B' form) prepared on a Grossbogen/table format. Filed electronically through the authorised cantonal e-filing portal (Zug Steueramt eTax or a listed fiscal software such as WINTAX, Abacus, or SwissTax) which sends the federal calculation to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional direct federal tax and cantonal tax instalments are payable quarterly during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Standard filing deadline: 30 June following the closed financial year (i.e. within six months after balance-sheet date), with extensions of up to six months available on written request; for calendar-year AGs, the tax return is generally delivered between February and April and assessed by the cantonal authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, legal form (AG), commercial register number, Swiss UID number, place of effective administration and mailing address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident AG taxed only on Swiss-source income must state its foreign registered office and the Swiss permanent establishment (Betriebsstätte) address separately; no domestic domicile is entered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered share capital, nominal value per share, and list of resolutions for capital contributions (reserve from paid-in capital).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the non-resident shareholding percentage; this information is used for participation deduction and withholding-tax refund eligibility under DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit per commercial profit and loss account (Handelsbilanzgewinn) before allocation to reserves, after depreciation and provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident companies with Swiss PE, enter the profit attributable to the Swiss permanent establishment in accordance with the OECD-compliant separate enterprise principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses disallowed in tax accounting: dividend withholding tax, federal/cantonal taxes, interest on hidden equity, 50% of board fees to related parties, penalties and non-commercial gifts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs must add all expenses deducted in the Swiss PE financial statements which are not allocable to Swiss-source taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-recognised depreciation using the official Swiss depreciation tables (Mfrb. Br. 001) for machinery, moulds, airbrush tooling and website IP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Depreciation of assets forming part of a Swiss PE of a non-resident may be applied in the PE accounts only; assets booked offshore cannot be depreciated in the Swiss return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest on shareholder loans, bank debt and finance leases; also thin-capitalisation debt ratio and interest-rate review for hidden equity distribution.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid by a Swiss PE to its foreign head office is non-deductible except where a constructive inland capitalisation applies and the loan carries arm's-length coupons.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 – IP income and patent box
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net qualifying IP income (patents, equivalent IP, software copyright) eligible for up to 90% exemption under the Swiss patent box regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident owning Swiss IP via a Swiss PE can claim the patent-box relief on the PE taxable profit; no relief is available for IP held and managed offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issuance agio and other paid-in capital reserves that can be repaid tax-free and without Swiss dividend withholding tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only audited and documented paid-in capital (capital contribution reserves) is excluded from withholding tax; repayments must be recorded in the Swiss commercial register.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: procedural fine under Art. 175 DBG of up to CHF 10,000, escalated on second offence up to CHF 30,000; default interest at 4.5% per annum accrues on underpaid tax, and tax authorities may assess tax by estimation from third-party data. If the return is filed after formal reminder, cantonal procedural penalties of approximately CHF 50–200 per week can additionally be imposed. Criminal sanctions for tax fraud/incomplete filings can reach five years imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Swiss statutory dividend withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) is 35% on gross distributions by a Swiss AG. Treaty-reduced rates using DTA protocol: 0% for a qualifying corporate shareholder holding at least 10% of voting power (subject to MLI Principal Purpose Test); 5% for holdings ≥10% where the treaty provides; 15% for most portfolio investors. Repayment of capital contribution reserves (agio) is exempt from Swiss WHT where properly audited.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from a DTA rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must file Form 820 (Antrag um Auszahlung/Nachforderung der Verrechnungssteuer) with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration within three years of the end of the dividend year, attaching the original Tax Residence Certificate (TRC), a statement of the Swiss company's share-distribution notification, proof of common shareholding and of beneficial ownership, and a declaration that the shareholder has no permanent establishment in Switzerland. For an interim refund before the tax assessment, Form 823 (Vorauszahlung) can be filed. The FTA checks substance, source of funds and MLI/PPT; refunds are denied to letterbox companies or conduit shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Switzerland levies no statutory withholding tax on cross-border royalties or ordinary business interest. Interest paid by a Swiss AG on a shareholder loan or a bond is subject to 35% WHT only if the instrument is considered taxable Swiss debt (e.g. publicly issued bonds or a liability recorded with a Swiss paying agent); international loans between Swiss and foreign companies are exempt from WHT. Royalties for patents, designs, software and similar IP are WHT-exempt and no treaty relief is necessary, but transfer-pricing deductibility remains under OECD guidelines.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Switzerland has not codified an explicit statutory threshold in the Federal Direct Tax Act. In practice, the tax administration applies a materiality benchmark of CHF 1,000,000 annual aggregate intercompany turnover (goods/services/IP/interest) for requiring a Local File; a Master File is expected where the Swiss group entity has cross-border related-party transactions in excess of CHF 10,000,000 or where the international group turnover exceeds CHF 50,000,000. Swiss CbCR is mandatory for groups with consolidated annual revenue of CHF 900,000,000 or more. Contemporaneous documentation must be completed within the statutory deadlines (tax return preparation time) and in any event before final tax assessment.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no Economic Substance Regulations akin to the UAE/Caribbean regimes. However, economic substance is an implicit self-standing principle applied through (i) Art. 58 DBG proper and complete commercial books, (ii) the EU/OECD Principal Purpose Test and Multilateral Instrument (MLI) treaty-abuse rules, (iii) the tax administration's transfer-pricing functional analysis, and (iv) the Federal Court practice under which an artificial legal arrangement without genuine business purpose is disregarded. An AG must maintain a real location, employees/board meetings in Switzerland, assume operative risks and own functional assets; otherwise tax authorities may recharacterise intercompany transactions, deny expense deductions, treat royalty or interest flows as hidden profit distributions, and refuse WHT refunds under DTA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-reporting gross sales from designer blind box toys by diverting payments from Shopify/Stripe/local card terminals to private crypto wallets or off-book PayPal accounts; creating fictitious purchase invoices from sham airbrush/rotocasting suppliers; declaring personal expenses as business costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax evasion under Art. 175 DBG: payment of the evaded tax plus a fine equal to one-quarter to twice the evaded amount; on aggravated professional tax evasion, fine up to CHF 500,000 and imprisonment up to five years. Under federal criminal law, value confiscation and disgorgement of the non-taxed profit is ordered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who falsely sign the corporate tax return are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid Federal and cantonal tax claim if they caused the evasion intentionally or negligently; they may be prosecuted as perpetrator or abettor and face personal fines, seizure of their Swiss bank accounts and, in aggravated fraud cases, a departure ban (travel ban) pending criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing a profit-dividend from the Swiss AG to a foreign beneficial owner without deducting and remitting the 35% statutory withholding tax, or disguising the distribution as repayment of capital contribution reserves using unaudited fictitious paid-in capital accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 12 Verrechnungssteuergesetz (VStG) the AG is liable for the full 35% tax not collected, plus 5% default interest and procedure costs; intentional non-payment triggers a criminal fine up to CHF 30,000 and, on conviction, confiscation of equivalent hidden reserves.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The board of directors is jointly and severally liable for the withholding tax liability to the Federal Tax Administration in case of payment inability of the AG; individual board members who signed the payment instructions can be named as debtors in administrative enforcement proceedings and are subject to asset attachment, prohibition to serve as a director in Switzerland and, if the tax debt is large, criminal seizure of private assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Converting the AG into a letterbox entity: no staff or office in Switzerland, all decisions taken by a foreign parent/trust, intercompany royalties routed to a Monaco/Dubai IP shell, and Swiss tax returns exposing only minimal net profit while the Swiss entity pays out high management fees to a related-party service provider.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the arrangement under Swiss substance and TP rules: management fees, royalties and interest reclassified as non-deductible hidden profit distributions; additional Swiss corporate income tax and 35% WHT assessed on the recharacterized amounts; penalties of 10–100% of the evaded direct tax; DTA refunds, including any treaty protections, are denied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The de facto and de jure directors are personally liable for the company's tax debts to the extent that assets were diverted to the foreign shell after the debt arose; civil veil-piercing is granted in case of significant undercapitalisation and fraudulent intent, leading to personal restitution orders, freezing of personal Swiss real estate and bank balances, and, for non-resident directors, entry bans to Schengen territory.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting customer payments in cryptocurrency or via anonymous third-party payment links without customer due diligence, deliberately concealing that the Shopify/Stripe proceeds are ultimately settled to the account of a politically exposed person or a sanctioned ultimate beneficial owner in a non-cooperative jurisdiction; structuring local POS cash withdrawals into below-reporting-threshold transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG/AMLA) Art. 37: fine up to CHF 500,000; laundering of criminal funds under Art. 305bis Swiss Criminal Code carries imprisonment up to three years (five years in qualified cases), with confiscation of assets and publication of judgment; a legal entity may be ordered to pay compensation not exceeding the amount of the laundered value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who design the payment routing or knowingly tolerate the omission of beneficial-owner identification are individually criminally liable and can be imprisoned; their personal fiduciary or corporate assets are attachable, and a travel ban is imposed by the investigation judge where there is a risk of collusion or flight.
